extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology record from primary results text, figure captions, and supplement DOCX; claims are bounded to evidence strength.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Temporin-G directly interferes with influenza PR8 hemagglutination and low-pH RBC hemolysis in source assays, supporting interaction with viral HA and impaired HA2 conformational rearrangement.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Temporin-G against influenza A PR8 hemagglutinin/HA-mediated entry

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=25:The antiviral activity of TG is related to the peptide ability to prevent the conformational change in the viral HA2 subunit; xml:fig=6:FIGURE 6

mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct biochemical/cell-free assays support HA interaction/fusion inhibition context but do not alone map all residue-level contacts.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Docking and HADDOCK refinement support a model in which Temporin-G occupies the HA1/HA2 stem groove; this is computational support, not a standalone direct mechanism.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=26:TG binds HA stem groove at the HA1/HA2 interface; xml:fig=7:FIGURE 7

mechanism_claims.limitations: Computational model is preserved as supportive evidence and not promoted above the in vitro HA assays.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Time-of-addition, attachment/entry, viral titer, ICW, and western blot assays support an influenza entry-phase phenotype for Temporin-G treatment.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Temporin-G against influenza A PR8 in A549 cells

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=23:Treatment with TG affects influenza virus replication; xml:sec=24:Temporin G inhibits the entry of influenza virus into the host cells; xml:fig=2:FIGURE 2; xml:fig=3:FIGURE 3; xml:fig=4:FIGURE 4

mechanism_claims.limitations: Phenotype supports entry-phase inhibition but exact figure bar heights beyond textual log/percent summaries are not over-digitized.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: For Sendai virus, Temporin-G reduces released viral titer while HN expression is not reduced in the POST condition, supporting a late-release/budding-stage phenotype rather than entry blockade.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Temporin-G against Sendai virus in A549 cells
